summary:
“ Tok Tam” revolves around a group of animal who live in a small Malaysian Village. They lives in a barn led by an old wise Turkey, Tok Tam. Along with him there are the family of Jaguh the rooster, Bu the hen and their chicks, Chick and Chack. There are also Misai the cat, Mak Boo the cow, Pak Bekk the goat, Cik Lenggang the duck and Cik Siti the mouse. In the series, Tok Tam will tell moral stories fill with message and values for the viewers. Among the stories that will be told are.The Rabbit and The Tortoise, The Greedy Lion, The Wise Mousedeer and others.

In every episode, you will also be entertained with folk song from the region. The song will be presented with dances and sketches perform by the animation characters from the series. The series will also potray advice and guidance in a special segment with Tok Tam on safety measures such as how to cross the roads, handling electrical appliances and others. Meanwhile, Professor Jampuk the Owl and friends, will teach alphabets A to Z and introduce shapes and colors. Insanely Simple : The Obsession That Drives Apples's Success
author: Segall, Ken
summary: Simplicity isn't just a design principle at Apple--it's a value that permeates every level of the organization. The obsession with simplicity is what separates Apple from other technology companies. It's what helped Apple recover from near death in 1997 to become the most valuable company on Earth in 2011. Thanks to Steve Jobs' uncompromising ways, you can see simplicity in everything APple does: the way it's structured, the way it innovates, and the way it speaks to its customers. It's by crushing the forces of complexity that the company remains on its stellar trajectory. As ad agency creative director, Ken Segall played a key role in Apple's resurrection, helping to create such critical marketing campaigns as Think different. By naming the iMac, he also laid the foundation for naming waves of i-products to come. Segall has a unique perspective, given his years of experience creating campaigns for other iconic tech companies, including IBM, Intel, and Dell. It was the stark contrast of Apple's ways that made Segall appreciate the power of simplicity--and inspired him to help others benefit from it
